predecessors.name: Scandinavian minor kingdoms
predecessors.text: the Mälaren core that Cliopatria cuts out of its Scandinavian minor kingdoms row in 980 (145.8 k km2 in 960-979, 117.7 k km2 from 980)

ledger.x: 980: a unified Swedish kingdom emerges in the Mälaren lands.

c. 1000: Olof Skötkonung rules the Svear and the Geats. S3: 'Around the year 1000, Olof Skötkonung became the first known king to rule both Svealand and Götaland.' The year is approximate; the land is the part of the minor kingdoms row that Cliopatria hands over in 1000.
1003: the rest of the old minor kingdoms block joins Sweden.
1220: a small coastal step east in south-west Finland.
1249-1250: the Second Swedish Crusade brings Tavastia under Sweden.

c. 1250: south-west Finland is Swedish. Page silent on a conquest date: S9 has evidence of Swedish rule 'from the middle of the 13th century onwards', Christianisation there that 'is known to have already started in the 10th century', and a first crusade of the 1150s that 'possibly in 1155, most likely never occurred'.
1293: the Third Swedish Crusade against the Karelians opens the struggle with Novgorod for the Karelian Isthmus.
1293: the western Karelian Isthmus round Vyborg becomes Swedish.
14th century: Ostrobothnia is brought into the realm.
12 August 1323: the Treaty of Nöteborg gives Sweden Savonia's border parishes.
12 August 1323: the Treaty of Nöteborg, signed at Oreshek, ends the struggle for the Karelian Isthmus.
1332: Magnus Eriksson buys Scania, Blekinge and Ven.
1337: Sweden attacks Korela and Viborg again.
1339: peace with Novgorod.
August 1348: Magnus takes Nöteborg (Oreshek) in his crusade.
February 1349: the Novgorodians retake Nöteborg.
1360: Valdemar IV of Denmark takes back Scania.
1360: Blekinge goes with Scania.
27 July 1361: Valdemar IV of Denmark takes Gotland.
18 February 1364: Albert of Mecklenburg is proclaimed and crowned king of Sweden.
17 June 1397: Sweden joins Norway and Denmark in the Kalmar Union.
20 June 1448: Sweden elects its own king and leaves the Kalmar Union.
23 June 1457: Christian I of Denmark becomes king of Sweden and the union is restored.
June 1464: Christian I loses Sweden.
6 October 1497: Hans wins Sweden back.
August 1501: the Swedish council renounces Hans.
November 1520: Christian II is crowned king of Sweden.
January 1521: the Swedish War of Liberation begins.
6 June 1523: the Swedes make Gustav Vasa their king and leave the Kalmar Union.
6 June 1523: 'Gustav Eriksson (Vasa) was proclaimed King of Sweden at the Riksdag in Strängnäs on 6 June 1523'; 'Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523'; 'Stockholm was taken on 17 June.'
June 1523: the Swedish realm leaves the Kalmar Union for good.
June 1561: Reval and northern Estonia place themselves under Swedish protection.
1564: the Swedes occupy Jämtland and Härjedalen.
1570: the Long Wrath against Russia opens.
13 December 1570: 'peace was finally reached on 13 December 1570 with the Treaty of Stettin'; 'These provinces were later regained by Denmark-Norway following the peace process in 1570.'
1580: Kexholm falls to Sweden.
1581: 'a mercenary army hired by Sweden recaptured the strategic city of Narva'.
10 August 1583: the Truce of Plussa gives Sweden most of Ingria.
February 1590: Sweden loses Ingria.
18 May 1595: the Treaty of Teusina ends the war.
18 May 1595: Sweden gives up Kexholm.

wars.name: Swedish-Novgorodian wars to the Treaty of Nöteborg
wars.outcome: Treaty of Nöteborg, 12 August 1323: an 18-point frontier from south of Viborg Castle to 'Kajano more'; Novgorod cedes the pogosts of Savilahti, Jääski and Äyräpää; northern Ostrobothnia and Lapland left as common land.

wars.name: Swedish attack on Korela and Viborg
wars.outcome: Peace in 1339; the Treaty of Nöteborg renewed with a clause on escaping Karelians; no frontier change.

wars.name: Magnus Eriksson's crusade against Novgorod
wars.outcome: Nöteborg taken in August 1348 and retaken by Novgorod in February 1349 after a six-month siege.

wars.name: Valdemar IV's reconquest of Scania and Gotland
wars.outcome: Valdemar reconquered Scania in 1360 and won a complete victory outside Visby, Gotland, on 27 July 1361: Scania and Gotland pass to Denmark (Blekinge goes with Scania).

wars.name: Swedish War of Liberation (Gustav Vasa's rebellion against the Kalmar Union)
wars.outcome: Gustav Vasa, appointed commander over Dalarna in January 1521, was recognised as leader of Sweden at Vadstena in August 1521; Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523, he was proclaimed king at Strängnäs on 6 June 1523 and Stockholm was taken on 17 June; the Treaty of…

wars.name: Livonian War, Sweden's part
wars.outcome: Sweden kept the lands that sought its protection in 1561 and captured Narva; the Treaty of Plussa of 1583 left it in control of northern Estonia and Dagö.

wars.name: Long Wrath (Russo-Swedish war of 1570-1595)
wars.outcome: Ended by the Treaty of Teusina in 1595; S3 has Ingria and Kexholm ceded to Russia in 1590.

wars.name: Northern Seven Years' War (Sweden against Denmark-Norway and Lübeck)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Stettin, 13 December 1570: 'Status quo ante bellum in Scandinavia'; Jämtland and Härjedalen, occupied by Sweden from 1564, returned to Denmark-Norway; the Swedish king withdrew the claims to Norway, Skåne, Halland, Blekinge and Gotland.

certainty.note: Forest and coast frontiers without lines; the Finnish and Karelian edges are crusade limits.
